# Tatton Projects

> Tatton Projects is an owner-managed construction contractor based in Altrincham, Cheshire. It delivers commercial fit-out and refurbishment UK-wide, and new build homes, housing developments and major home extensions across Greater Manchester and Cheshire. 110+ projects and £8m delivered since 2020.

- Owner-managed: the person who priced the job is the person managing it on site. Founded in 2020 by Dave Groom (founder and contracts manager).
- Builds around live operations: care homes, hotels, surgeries, restaurants, shops and occupied offices that stay open during the works.
- Accreditations and memberships: Federation of Master Builders, Constructionline Gold, CITB, CSCS.
- Areas: Manchester, Altrincham, Hale, Bowdon, Knutsford, Wilmslow, Alderley Edge, Sale, Stockport, Macclesfield, Chester and the rest of Greater Manchester and Cheshire; commercial fit-out and refurbishment anywhere in the UK.

## Services

### Office Fit-Out Manchester
URL: https://www.tatton-projects.co.uk/office-fit-out-manchester

Tatton Projects delivers office fit-outs, workplace refurbishments and commercial interior projects across Manchester, Greater Manchester and the North West, with selected projects delivered nationwide.

Our approach combines practical construction delivery with programme, procurement and commercial management. We work with clients, architects, engineers, Building Control and specialist subcontractors to turn an agreed scope into a controlled construction project.

Most of our fit-outs happen in buildings that stay open — floors handed back in phases, dust and route separation, noisy trades out of hours. A recent multi-floor £2M Cat B fit-out was delivered floor by floor in a live, occupied building.

2026 guide prices: Cat A refresh £45–£70 / sq ft; Cat B — standard £70–£110 / sq ft; Cat B — high spec £110–£180+ / sq ft; Occupied building +10–25% (All-in, excluding VAT and loose furniture. Manchester and the North West.)

- Cat A & Cat B office fit-out: We undertake Cat A landlord works and Cat B occupier fit-outs, including partitions, ceilings, flooring, lighting, power, data, mechanical services, kitchens, breakout spaces, bespoke joinery and finishes.
- Pre-construction that reduces surprises: Before mobilisation we review drawings, specifications, landlord requirements, programme, access, long-lead items, M&E requirements and the cost plan so key risks are identified early.
- One accountable project team: Tatton Projects coordinates procurement, subcontractors, programme, health and safety, quality, variations, snagging and handover through one project team.
- Manchester and UK-wide commercial delivery: We work across Manchester, Trafford, Salford, Stockport, Altrincham, Cheshire and the wider North West, with selected commercial fit-out projects delivered nationwide.

Q: What does an office fit-out cost per square foot in Manchester?
A: As a working range in 2026: a basic Cat A refresh runs around £45–£70 per sq ft. A standard Cat B fit-out is roughly £70–£110 per sq ft. A high-specification Cat B — bespoke joinery, feature lighting, acoustic treatment, the kind of thing we did at Sentric Music — runs £110–£180 per sq ft and upwards. Anyone who quotes you a single number without seeing the floor, the building's services and the landlord's licence to alter is guessing. We give you an elemental cost plan instead, and that number is the one you build to.

Q: Can you work in my building while we're still open?
A: Yes — it's most of what we do. Hotels that kept selling rooms, care homes with residents in their beds, a public service centre with ninety staff at their desks and the public coming through the doors, retail units in a trading mall. Phased handbacks, dust and route separation, out-of-hours working. If you can only close for a weekend, say so at the appraisal and we'll build the programme around it.

Q: How do you stop the final account creeping?
A: A written cost plan at stage two and a signed variation procedure before anyone lifts a spade. Written variations only — no verbal extras, ever. Monthly valuations so you always know where the number is.

Q: Do you work outside Manchester?
A: Yes. Commercial fit-out and refurbishment we take nationwide for the right project. We have delivered in Liverpool, Leeds, Stockport and London.

### Commercial Refurbishment Manchester
URL: https://www.tatton-projects.co.uk/commercial-refurbishment-manchester

Tatton Projects delivers commercial refurbishment across Manchester and the North West, coordinating the building fabric, interiors and specialist trades required to upgrade existing workplaces and commercial property.

Our approach combines practical construction delivery with programme, procurement and commercial management. We work with clients, architects, engineers, Building Control and specialist subcontractors to turn an agreed scope into a controlled construction project.

If your building is EPC E, in most cases it can't lawfully be let. We survey it, tell you what it costs to get the rating up, and do the work — often fabric, lighting and controls rather than anything dramatic.

At a glance: Buildings Occupied or vacant; Phasing Around your operation; EPC & MEES Survey, cost, upgrade

- Refurbishment without losing control of the building: Existing buildings bring unknowns. We plan surveys, enabling works, sequencing, temporary protection, procurement and interfaces with existing services before the main programme gathers pace.
- Occupied and phased works: Where a client remains operational, works can be planned in phases with access, noise, dust and service interruptions considered in the programme.
- One team across the trades: We coordinate strip-out, partitions, ceilings, flooring, joinery, decoration, M&E, fire stopping and associated builders work.
- From brief to handover: Tatton Projects can support pre-construction review, cost planning, delivery, snagging and handover, providing a clear point of responsibility throughout the refurbishment.

Q: My building is EPC E. Can I still let it?
A: Not lawfully, in most cases — and the standard is tightening. This is the MEES regime, and it turns an aesthetic decision into a legal one: a sub-standard building can't earn until it's fixed. We survey it, tell you what it costs to get the rating up, and do the work. Often it's fabric, lighting and controls rather than anything dramatic. Get it assessed before your next void, not during one.

Q: Can you work in my building while we're still open?
A: Yes — it's most of what we do. Hotels that kept selling rooms, care homes with residents in their beds, a public service centre with ninety staff at their desks and the public coming through the doors, retail units in a trading mall. Phased handbacks, dust and route separation, out-of-hours working.

Q: How do you stop the final account creeping?
A: A written cost plan at stage two and a signed variation procedure before anyone lifts a spade. Written variations only — no verbal extras, ever. Monthly valuations so you always know where the number is.

### New Build Homes Cheshire
URL: https://www.tatton-projects.co.uk/new-build-homes-cheshire

Tatton Projects delivers new-build homes across Cheshire and Greater Manchester, coordinating the construction process from pre-construction and groundworks through structure, services, finishes and handover.

Our approach combines practical construction delivery with programme, procurement and commercial management. We work with clients, architects, engineers, Building Control and specialist subcontractors to turn an agreed scope into a controlled construction project.

Our Knutsford new build — an empty plot to a finished family home in brick and flint under a slate roof — came in at circa £400,000 for the build.

2026 guide prices: Good standard £2,000–£2,600 / sq m; High specification £2,600–£3,800 / sq m; Exceptional £3,800–£5,500+ / sq m; Basement £3,000–£5,000 / sq m (Finished floor area, excluding VAT, land, professional fees and abnormals. Cheshire and Greater Manchester.)

- A managed route from drawings to site: We review architectural and structural information, procurement, programme, Building Control requirements and long-lead packages before and during delivery.
- From groundworks to finishes: Our scope can coordinate groundworks, structure, envelope, roofing, windows, M&E, internal finishes, kitchens, bathrooms and external works.
- Private clients and development: Tatton Projects works on substantial one-off homes and residential schemes where programme, quality and commercial control need active management.
- Cheshire and Greater Manchester: Our residential construction focus includes Knutsford, Wilmslow, Altrincham, Hale, Bowdon and surrounding Cheshire locations.

Q: What does a new build house cost per square metre in Cheshire?
A: As a 2026 guide: £2,000–£2,600 per square metre for a well-built family house at a good standard, £2,600–£3,800 for high specification, and £3,800–£5,500 and upwards for the exceptional — basement, pool or spa, lift, gated approach. That excludes VAT, land, professional fees and abnormals. A 220 sq m house at a good standard is roughly £506,000 for the build, and £580,000 to £620,000 all-in before land.

Q: I own a plot but don't know what it's worth. Can you help?
A: Send us the location and a title plan. You'll get a residual land value and a build cost back in five working days, free. If the numbers don't work we'll tell you that too — that advice is free, and it's cheaper than finding out after you've bought it.

Q: How do you stop the final account creeping?
A: A written cost plan at stage two and a signed variation procedure before anyone lifts a spade. Written variations only — no verbal extras, ever. Monthly valuations so you always know where the number is.

Q: Where do you build?
A: New build homes, developments and private work across Greater Manchester and Cheshire — Altrincham, Hale, Bowdon, Knutsford, Mobberley, Wilmslow, Alderley Edge, Sale, Timperley, Mere, Handforth, Northwich, Macclesfield, Lymm, Winsford, New Mills and Chester.

### Extension Builders Altrincham
URL: https://www.tatton-projects.co.uk/extension-builders-altrincham

Tatton Projects delivers substantial residential extensions, structural remodelling and complete property refurbishments across Altrincham, Hale, Bowdon and the surrounding Cheshire area.

Our approach combines practical construction delivery with programme, procurement and commercial management. We work with clients, architects, engineers, Building Control and specialist subcontractors to turn an agreed scope into a controlled construction project.

Tatton Projects is owner-managed, so the projects we take get proper attention — the person who priced the job is the person managing it on site. Extensions, remodels and whole-house refurbishments are all welcome.

2026 guide prices: Extension £2,400–£3,600 / sq m; Whole-house refurbishment £1,400–£2,800 / sq m; Basement £3,000–£5,000 / sq m (Finished floor area, excluding VAT, professional fees and abnormals. Cheshire and Greater Manchester.)

- Built for substantial projects: A major extension involves structure, foundations, drainage, glazing, M&E, kitchens and finishes. We manage the sequence and coordination rather than treating each package as an isolated trade.
- From drawings to construction: If you already have an architect and structural information, we can review the package, develop the construction scope and price the works. At an earlier stage, we can coordinate with the professional team to move the project towards site.
- Project-specific cost planning: Ground conditions, steelwork, glazing, kitchens, bathrooms, access and specification can materially change cost. We develop the price around the actual project rather than relying on a headline square-metre rate.
- Local coverage: Residential work is focused on Altrincham, Hale, Bowdon and the wider Greater Manchester and Cheshire area.

Q: How much does an extension cost per square metre?
A: As a 2026 guide across Cheshire and Greater Manchester: £2,400–£3,600 per square metre for a single or two-storey extension with structural alterations, tying into the existing house. It often costs more per square metre than a new build, because nothing is square. Whole-house refurbishment runs £1,400–£2,800 per square metre. Rates exclude VAT, professional fees and abnormals — ground conditions, drainage diversions and structural surprises are found by survey, not by a rate.

Q: Can you work from my architect's drawings?
A: Yes. If you already have an architect and structural information, we can review the package, develop the construction scope and price the works. At an earlier stage, we can coordinate with the professional team to move the project towards site.

Q: Which areas do you cover?
A: Altrincham, Hale, Bowdon and the wider Greater Manchester and Cheshire area — including Knutsford, Wilmslow, Alderley Edge, Sale, Timperley, Mere, Lymm and Macclesfield.

### Cat A & Cat B Fit-Out
URL: https://www.tatton-projects.co.uk/cat-a-cat-b-fit-out

Tatton Projects delivers Cat A and Cat B office fit-out across the UK, from landlord Cat A upgrades that make a floor lettable to full Cat B fit-outs that turn a bare shell into a workplace.

Cat A is the landlord's base build: raised floors, suspended ceilings, basic services, fire detection and finished surfaces that leave a floor clean, lettable and ready for a tenant. Cat B is the tenant's fit-out: the layout, partitions, meeting rooms, kitchens, joinery, branding, lighting and workplace design that turn that empty floor into somewhere a team actually works.

We deliver both, and the shell-to-handover work in between, coordinating landlord, tenant, designer and building control so the two stages meet cleanly instead of clashing on site.

Guide rates: Cat A refresh £45–£70 / sq ft; Standard Cat B £70–£110 / sq ft; High-spec Cat B £110–£180 / sq ft; Coverage UK-wide, selected (2026 guide rates, excluding VAT and professional fees. A measured cost plan replaces the range.)

- Cat A for landlords: Raised floors, ceilings, base services, fire detection and finished surfaces that make a floor lettable and pass a letting agent's inspection.
- Cat B for tenants: Space planning, partitions, meeting rooms, tea points, joinery, feature lighting, acoustics, branding and the full workplace fit-out.
- Shell-to-handover: A bare shell taken all the way to an occupied floor as one managed project, so nothing falls between landlord and tenant scope.
- Dilapidations & reinstatement: End-of-lease strip-out and reinstatement back to the Cat A condition your lease requires.

Q: What is the difference between Cat A and Cat B fit-out?
A: Cat A is the landlord's base finish, raised floors, ceilings, basic services and finished surfaces that make a floor lettable. Cat B is the tenant's fit-out on top: layout, partitions, meeting rooms, kitchens, joinery, lighting and branding. We deliver both.

Q: How much does a Cat B office fit-out cost?
A: As a 2026 guide: a Cat A refresh runs about £45–£70 per sq ft, a standard Cat B £70–£110, and a high-specification Cat B £110–£180 and up. We give you an elemental cost plan rather than a single headline number.

Q: Do you work UK-wide?
A: Yes. Commercial fit-out is delivered across the UK on selected projects, managed from Manchester with the same team on site wherever the building is.

Q: Can you take a shell through Cat A and Cat B as one project?
A: Yes. Running Cat A straight into Cat B as one programme avoids the gap where landlord and tenant scope usually clash, and gets the floor occupied sooner.

### Building & Change-of-Use Conversions
URL: https://www.tatton-projects.co.uk/building-conversions

Tatton Projects converts buildings to new uses, offices to apartments, commercial to residential and change-of-use projects under permitted development, from structural work through to finished, lettable space.

Conversions turn a building that no longer earns into one that does: offices into apartments, redundant commercial space into homes, and mixed change-of-use schemes. Many now proceed under permitted development rights such as Class MA, which lets suitable commercial premises become residential without a full planning application, though prior approval and building regulations still apply.

We handle the whole conversion: structural alterations, new floors and cores, services, fire compartmentation, acoustics, insulation and the finishes that make the space lettable or saleable.

At a glance: Office to residential Class MA & full planning; Commercial change of use Retail, industrial, mixed; Structure Alterations & new cores; Coverage UK-wide, selected (Permitted development still needs prior approval and building regulations sign-off. We confirm the route at survey.)

- Office to residential: Converting redundant offices into apartments, under Class MA permitted development or full planning.
- Commercial change of use: Retail, industrial and mixed-use buildings converted to a new, consented use.
- Structure & compartmentation: New floors, cores, fire compartmentation, acoustic separation and insulation to meet residential standards.
- Fit-out & finishes: Kitchens, bathrooms, services and finishes that leave units ready to let or sell.

Q: Can I convert an office into flats without planning permission?
A: Often, yes. Class MA permitted development lets many offices and commercial premises become residential without a full planning application, but you still need prior approval from the council and building regulations sign-off. We confirm the route at survey.

Q: What is change of use?
A: It is moving a building from one planning use class to another, for example commercial to residential. Some changes are permitted development, others need full planning. Either way the building work must meet building regulations.

Q: Do you do office-to-residential conversions?
A: Yes, converting redundant offices and commercial buildings into apartments is a core part of what we do, from structure and compartmentation through to finished, lettable units.

Q: Do you work UK-wide on conversions?
A: Commercial and mixed-use conversions are delivered on selected projects nationwide; residential conversion work is focused on Greater Manchester and Cheshire.

The programme is built around the building's routine, day rooms, medication rounds and clinics, so the works progress without putting residents or patients at risk.

At a glance: Settings Care homes, surgeries, clinics; Occupied Infection control & phasing; Compliance Fire, DDA, HTM-aware; Coverage UK-wide, selected

- Infection & dust control: Sealed zones, negative pressure where needed, HEPA extraction and rigorous cleaning regimes.
- Phased handbacks: Rooms and wings handed back in a planned sequence so the building keeps running.

Q: Can you work in an occupied care home?
A: Yes, it is what we specialise in. Works are zoned and sealed, dust and noise controlled, and rooms handed back in a planned sequence so residents stay safe and the home keeps running.

Q: Do you fit out GP surgeries and clinics?
A: Yes, GP, dental and clinical settings, delivered with the infection control, compartmentation and compliance these buildings require.

Q: Do you work UK-wide on healthcare projects?
A: Yes, healthcare fit-out and refurbishment is delivered on selected projects nationwide, managed from Manchester.

Q: How do you keep infection risk down during works?

### Builders in Altrincham

### House Renovations Altrincham
URL: https://www.tatton-projects.co.uk/house-renovations-altrincham

Period and inter-war houses across Altrincham, Hale and Bowdon taken back to brick and rebuilt inside: structure, services, glazing, kitchens, bathrooms, joinery and decoration under one contract and one programme.

A renovation touches every trade in the building at once. We sequence strip-out, structure, first fix, plastering, second fix and finishes so the house comes back together in the right order, and we manage Building Control, the structural engineer and specialist subcontractors as part of the job.

Most of our renovation work is Victorian, Edwardian and 1930s housing in Altrincham, Hale and Bowdon, often combined with a rear extension or a loft or basement conversion in the same contract.

2026 guide prices: Whole-house refurbishment £1,400–£2,800 / sq m; Extension £2,400–£3,600 / sq m; Basement £3,000–£5,000 / sq m (Finished floor area, excluding VAT, professional fees and abnormals. Altrincham, Cheshire and Greater Manchester.)

- Strip-out and structure: Back to brick where it needs it, with steels, openings and remodelled layouts designed and signed off before the first wall comes down.
- Services and fabric: New electrics, plumbing and heating, insulation and glazing, so the finished house performs as well as it looks.
- Kitchens, bathrooms and joinery: Bespoke and supplied kitchens, bathrooms, staircases, built-in wardrobes and fitted joinery, as in our Didsbury projects.
- Finishes and handover: Plaster, decoration, flooring and a snagged, cleaned handover with the paperwork for Building Control.

Q: How long does a whole-house renovation take?
A: It depends on the size of the house and how much structure changes, but a full renovation of a four-bedroom house, back to brick with new services, typically runs several months on site. We give you a dated programme with the cost plan and update it as the job progresses.

Q: Can we live in the house during the work?
A: For a full back-to-brick renovation it is usually better and cheaper to move out: the house has no services for a period and every room is a work area. For phased work we can plan around an occupied house, which we do routinely on commercial jobs.

Q: Do you handle planning and Building Control?
A: Internal renovation rarely needs planning permission, but extensions, loft and basement conversions and changes to a listed building or a house in a conservation area can. All structural and most services work needs Building Control approval, which we arrange and manage as part of the contract.

Q: Which areas do you cover for renovations?
A: Altrincham, Hale, Bowdon, Hale Barns, Timperley and Sale, and the wider Cheshire and south Manchester area including Wilmslow, Knutsford and Didsbury.

### Basement Conversions Altrincham
URL: https://www.tatton-projects.co.uk/basement-conversions-altrincham

Cellars and new basements beneath existing houses in Altrincham, Hale and Bowdon: structural underpinning, tanking and waterproofing, drainage, services and finished rooms such as cinema rooms, offices and lounges.

On tight plots and protected streets in Altrincham and Hale, going down is often the only way to add real floor area. A basement conversion underpins the existing structure, forms a waterproof envelope and brings in drainage, ventilation, heating and power before the rooms are finished to the standard of the house above.

Our Hale basement walkthrough shows the finished result: a cinema room, a home office and a lounge beneath an existing property. It is one of several basement projects we have delivered across Altrincham, Hale and Bowdon.

2026 guide prices: Basement £3,000–£5,000 / sq m; Extension £2,400–£3,600 / sq m; Whole-house refurbishment £1,400–£2,800 / sq m (Finished floor area, excluding VAT, professional fees and abnormals. Altrincham, Cheshire and Greater Manchester.)

- Structure and underpinning: The existing walls are underpinned in a controlled sequence, designed by a structural engineer and inspected by Building Control as the work progresses.
- Waterproofing: A designed waterproofing system, typically a cavity drain membrane with sump and pump or a tanked lining, so the space stays dry for the long term.
- Services and ventilation: Drainage, mechanical ventilation, heating, power, lighting and data brought in while the shell is open, with escape routes designed in.
- Finished rooms: Cinema rooms, offices, gyms, lounges and guest suites, finished to match the rest of the house.

Q: Does a basement conversion need planning permission?
A: Converting an existing cellar usually does not, as long as the outside of the house does not change and it is not a listed building. Digging a new basement, enlarging one, adding a lightwell or changing the external appearance usually does, and some Altrincham and Hale streets sit in conservation areas. We check this with you at cost-plan stage.

Q: Does it need Building Regulations approval?
A: Yes. Structure, waterproofing, fire escape, ventilation, damp-proofing and electrics are all covered by the Building Regulations, and the underpinning is inspected in stages. We arrange and manage this as part of the contract.

Q: Will I need a party wall agreement?
A: If the house is semi-detached or terraced, or the excavation is close to a neighbour's foundations, the Party Wall etc. Act 1996 almost always applies. We advise early so notices go out before the programme depends on them.

Q: How much does a basement cost?
A: As a 2026 working guide, £3,000–£5,000 per square metre of finished floor area, excluding VAT, professional fees and abnormals. Ground conditions, water table, access for muck away and the finish specification drive the number, so we price the actual house rather than a headline rate.
